I am 62 years old this year, and my knees ache when the weather turns damp, but I still get up before dawn to walk the fields. I have been farming these 13.1 mu for 40 years — since I was a young man — and I know every uneven spot. My household has seven people, but my two sons and my daughter-in-law work in a factory in the city. They send money home, which helps, but they are not here during the busy season, so the farm work falls mainly on me and my wife. I cannot afford to gamble.

I keep 10 mu for wheat-maize double cropping. That is the backbone of my farm. Last October I planted improved wheat seeds — the same kind my nephew used, and he had a good harvest. Now the wheat is greening up, so I will topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. I also put down compound fertilizer last autumn, about one bag per mu, so the phosphorus and potassium are already in the soil. This year I will irrigate three times: the return-green water now, one at jointing, and one when the grain is filling. Three times is what my neighbors do, and pumping from the well costs electricity, so I will not waste water. I will spray twice for pests — once for aphids when it warms up, and once if I see rust on the leaves. I rotary-tilled that land before planting last autumn.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, I plant hybrid maize immediately. The window is very tight — if I delay even a few days, the yield drops. I use no-tillage planting now. I hired a machine to do it last year and it saved me three days of back-breaking work, so I will do the same this year. I put down compound fertilizer as base, about 50 kg per mu, and topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations: one if June is dry, and one at tasseling. Summer rain usually helps. Two pesticide sprays.

I keep 2 mu for cotton. Cotton brings cash, and I need cash because my youngest son is saving to build a house. But cotton kills my back at picking time. My wife helps, and my daughter-in-law comes back from the factory in autumn, so between us we can manage 2 mu — no more. I plant improved Bt cotton in late April. I plough that field deep because cotton roots need to go deep. I give it about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and extra urea, especially potassium because cotton is greedy for it. Three irrigations: at flowering, at boll setting, and once more in August if the weather stays dry. Four pesticide sprays — even with Bt cotton, the sucking pests still come.

The remaining 1.1 mu I plant mungbean. I use my own seeds that I saved from last year — traditional seeds my father gave me long ago. Mungbean is easy; it does not need babysitting. I spread a small amount of compound fertilizer, about half a bag per mu, because mungbean makes its own nitrogen. One irrigation if the summer is very dry, and one spray if worms show up. I expect about 80 kg per mu. We eat some at home and sell the rest in the village market.

I thought about planting more cotton because the price was decent last year, but I am 62. I cannot manage more than 2 mu of cotton with just my wife and occasional help. The wheat and maize keep us fed, the cotton pays for the big expenses, and the mungbean is for small cash and eating. I watch every yuan I spend on inputs, but I will not starve my soil either — a bad harvest hurts more than saving a few kilograms of fertilizer.
